scenes.title: The problem
scenes.text: Taking crypto at checkout usually means: send tokens to this address. Then the merchant matches transfers to orders by hand. Wrong amounts slip through, and orders get marked paid on a screenshot.

scenes.title: What MezoCommerce is
scenes.text: MezoCommerce is checkout for stores on Mezo. Customers pay in MUSD, the Bitcoin-backed dollar, through a hosted page, a widget, or the API. Money goes straight to the merchant's wallet. We never hold it.

scenes.title: Merchant onboarding
scenes.text: A merchant signs in with their wallet, names the store, and registers it on Mezo. That's the only transaction setup needs. After it, MezoCommerce signs each checkout, with a key that can't change where the money goes.

scenes.title: Create a payment link
scenes.text: Now an order: 12.50 MUSD for a tin of tea. One click makes a payment link and a QR code. No wallet prompt.

scenes.title: Customer pays
scenes.text: The customer opens the link. The store, the amount and the payout wallet are locked in a signed payment intent. They sign one exact-amount permission and confirm one transaction.

scenes.title: Verified on-chain
scenes.text: The server reads the payment event on Mezo itself and waits for two confirmations. Only then is the order paid, with a link to the transaction.

scenes.title: Merchant dashboard
scenes.text: The merchant sees it in the dashboard, and their store can get a signed webhook. Refunds go back to the original payer, capped at what was paid.

scenes.title: How it works
scenes.text: Under the hood is one contract. A payment can't be paid twice. A wrong amount fails. And the contract never holds funds.

scenes.title: Live on Mezo testnet
scenes.text: It's live on Mezo testnet, with the contract source verified. Wallets connect through Mezo Passport, Bitcoin or Ethereum.

scenes.title: What's next
scenes.text: Next: a Shopify payments app, more tokens, and store plugins. MezoCommerce: sell beyond traditional payment rails.
